judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is a garbled fragment of an insuring clause ("\ill pey the proceeds cf this Folicy according to the ie sowing provisions"), so the promisor and the referenced provisions are not legible on the face of it. As an insuring agreement its substance is nevertheless conventional and points to the following sections for content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply incorporates the operative sections (4.1 Payment of Proceeds, Section 10 options) and does not contradict them. Nothing in Sections 4, 5 or 7 pulls against a bare promise to pay proceeds "according to the following provisions."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 20-day free-look wording is definite as to period, address and refund, apart from OCR noise; "void from the beginning" is a settled formula. No term here carries two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.1 (no coverage until premium paid) and 7.2 (Effective Date) — a refund on return is consistent with both. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision promises automatic paid-up level insurance at the anniversary following the insured's 95th birthday but the conditions list breaks off after "level amount based on: a. The current Policy Account Value less any Policy Indebtedness", leaving the amount of the level benefit undetermined. "Level amount based on" the account value is itself indeterminate as a benefit formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits awkwardly with Section 4.2, which fixes the death benefit by Coverage Option and the corridor table (which runs to age 95 at 100%), and with the Section 1 maturity/expiry dates; whether monthly charges and lapse under 5.10 continue after paid-up status is not addressed. That leaves a real reconciliation problem with the account-value machinery of Section 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The introduction is descriptive, but its statement that Sections 3 through 10 give "a more complete description of these rights" invites an argument about which text governs where a definition and an operative section differ. That is a mild interpretive hook rather than an ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the several defective cross-references in Section 2 (e.g. 2.15 pointing to "Section 4.3" for the Monthly Insurance Charge, which is 5.3), this priority statement could be invoked to subordinate the definitions. The tension is modest but real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of the Insured is a truncated fragment, but its intended sense — the person listed in Section 1 whose death causes proceeds to be paid — is not in doubt. Nothing ambiguous can be named beyond the OCR loss.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.2 (Owner may be someone other than the Insured) and 4.1. No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain definitional wording identifying "you" with the Owner and expressly allowing the Owner to differ from the Insured. No term is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 8.1–8.3 (Ownership, Change of Ownership, Assignment) and Section 1's designation of the Owner. Fully consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line identification of the insurer; nothing to construe. Only OCR garbling of the company name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cover page and 3.1's direction to pay premiums to "us". No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is cut off mid-sentence, so the mechanism for a subsequent change of beneficiary is not stated here. As written it fixes the beneficiary by the "original" application without qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.4, which supplies the default that the Owner is beneficiary if none is named and the change procedure; the definition is a summary of that and does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause defines Proceeds as amounts payable "as a result of the death of the Insured or upon surrender of the Policy while this Policy is in force and the Insured is alive"; the trailing condition is ambiguous as to which limb it qualifies. That is a namable syntactic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 separates Surrender Value (payable if the Insured is living and the Policy in force) from Death Proceeds, which resolves most of it. Residual tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite calendrical definition; the only defect is the truncated reference to Section 1. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.17 (Monthly Due Date is the same day as the Policy Date) and 7.2. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a pure signpost to Sections 7.2, 6.2 and the riders; its wording carries no independent uncertainty beyond OCR loss. "The date coverage commences" is a settled formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.2, which makes the effective date the later of the Policy Date or payment of the Minimum Initial Premium, and against 3.1's "no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made" — those two are themselves in mild tension, which this definition inherits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a clause fragment survives ("upon the Insured's age on the birthday nearest the first..."), so the age-determination rule cannot be applied as printed. An age definition that cannot be read is a genuine textual defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Age drives the 5.4 rate table and the 4.2 corridor percentages, but nothing in those provisions contradicts a nearest-birthday convention. No specific conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition combines an elective premium ("the amount and frequency you most recently elect") with a mandatory floor for two years, and says values "may, in turn, affect the amount and duration of insurance coverage" — permissive and mandatory language sit together. "Minimum that must be paid" against "you may make premium payments at any time and in any amount" is a namable tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.2(1)–(2) and 5.10's no-lapse rule for the first two years: the three provisions use slightly different formulations of the same two-year floor, so a reader must harmonise them. That is a real but resolvable reconciliation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite definition tied to a figure in Section 1. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1, 3.2(2) and 7.1's consideration clause. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is fragmentary, losing the words that tie the Specified Amount to the application and to death benefit determination. Its intended content is nonetheless standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2, 6.2 and 5.9's reduction of the Specified Amount on withdrawal under Option A. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition points to Section 4.2 for content and states only that the benefit depends on the Specified Amount and Coverage Option. Nothing independently ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 4.2's two options and the corridor table. No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence says both options give an increased death benefit "when the difference between the Policy Account Value and the death benefit reaches a minimum size" — "a minimum size" is left unquantified in the definition itself. That is a namable vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2's risk-percentage table supplies the actual corridor, so the vagueness is cured elsewhere in the instrument. Only slight residual tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The wording of the charge itself is definite (Cost of Insurance plus rider costs, deducted on each Monthly Due Date for the month just ended). No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference "See Section 4.3" is wrong: the Monthly Insurance Charge is dealt with in 5.3, while 4.3 is Interest on Death Proceeds. A misdirected internal reference is a genuine, if minor, coherence defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the cost of "pure insurance protection" using current rates and excludes rider costs; "pure insurance protection" is conventional and 5.4 supplies the formula. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.4 and 5.5, which separate rider charges. Cross-reference is correct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite date convention tied to the Policy Date; no ambiguity, and the truncated "See Sec 5" is OCR loss only. Nothing namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.6, 5.3 and 5.10's monthly test for lapse. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "There is no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made" is absolute, and the alternative "Planned Periodic Premium or Minimum Initial Premium" leaves which payment triggers coverage slightly open. The disjunctive is a namable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2 makes coverage effective on the later of the Policy Date or payment, and preserves any Temporary Insurance Agreement given when the application was taken; the flat "no coverage until payment" here sits in tension with that temporary-insurance carve-out. That is a specific pairing a court could be asked to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory lead-in that expressly subordinates the flexible-premium right to the four listed conditions. Definite in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.9 and with the enumerated sub-paragraphs that follow. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only the opening and closing words survive ("The total of your premium payments during... Premium shown in Section I"), so the two-year floor cannot be read off the provision as printed. Unreadable as a standalone obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its evident content duplicates 2.9 and 3.2(2); those supply the same floor, so there is no substantive inconsistency. No conflict found.
judgments.clause_name: 3.2(1) - Total of premium payments in first two policy years

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The month-by-month test ("one-twelfth of the Planned Periodic Premium on an annual basis multiplied by the number of elapsed Policy months") is arithmetically specified, though dense. No genuinely ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates almost, but not exactly, the no-lapse test in the last paragraph of 5.10, which additionally subtracts Partial Withdrawals and Policy Indebtedness; the two two-year tests must be harmonised. That is a specific, identifiable overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite floor on remittances plus a unilateral right to change it on notice; "we may change... at any time" is broad but plain. Nothing ambiguous to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.9's reference to the Minimum Premium Remittance in Section 1. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph mixes limits on amount, number of additional premiums and increases in Planned Periodic Premium, then adds "This will happen only if payment... would... increase the difference between the death benefit and the Policy Account Value" — the antecedent of "this" and the reach of the insurability condition are both unclear. That is a namable general-versus-specific and referential ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.3 (tax-qualification limit) and 4.2's corridor: the corridor mechanics explain why a premium could widen the gap, so the clause is broadly coherent. Residual tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tax-qualification limit is expressed by reference to external statutes (TEFRA, "Section 101F" of the Code) and "any future applicable regulations", and the insurer may "refuse to accept" or "return" excess premium — the scope of the limit is fixed by outside law rather than by the text. Some indeterminacy is inherent but the mechanism is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the unlimited premium right in 3.2 and complements 4.2's power to modify death benefits for tax compliance; those fit together. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The OCR has transposed the lead-in, but the operative terms — reinstatement within five years after expiry of the Grace Period, before surrender, on written request — are identifiable. The garbling leaves the trigger sentence hard to read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.10(2) (termination without value) and 7.8's two-year contest period for reinstatements. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A truncated condition ("Receipt of evidence of insurability of th..."), leaving whose insurability and to what standard unstated on its face. Elsewhere the policy uses "satisfactory to us", which is a discretionary standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels 6.2's requirement of "evidence of insurability satisfactory to us"; consistent with the instrument. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite quantum — premium sufficient for at least the next two Monthly Insurance Charges. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to "Section 5.2" is wrong; Monthly Insurance Charges are described in 5.3, and 5.2 is the Interest Rate provision. A minor misdirection within the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any Policy Indebtedness which existed at the end of the Grace Period will be reinstated, if it is not paid" is plain, though the conditional is loosely placed. No real second meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.4 (indebtedness deducted from proceeds) and with 3.4(4)'s use of lapse-date values. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States which values are used on reinstatement in definite terms; "Surrender Charges" tracks the Section 1 surrender-fee schedule. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 expresses the charge as a "Percent of Surrender Fee" schedule and 5.6 calls it a "Surrender Fee", so terminology varies slightly, but the reference is workable. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence ends at "will be the Monit", so the effective date of reinstatement is simply missing from the text. An unfinished operative date term is a defect on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Other provisions (6.2, 6.3) consistently use "the Monthly Due Date following" approval, which supplies the likely completion. No inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated at "returned for its S[urrender Value]", but the bar on reinstatement after surrender is clear in substance. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.8 (all insurance terminates on surrender) and 3.4's lead-in. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "We will pay the Surrender Value to you if the Insured is living and this Policy is in force" reads as an unconditional present obligation rather than one triggered by a surrender request. That mismatch between condition and trigger is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.8 makes surrender elective on written request and permits postponement for six months, so this sentence must be read as subject to 5.8; a literal reading would conflict with it. That is a specific pairing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short spendthrift statement qualified by "to the extent permitted by law". Definite in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.3 (assignment) and 8.4. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading sentence survives only in fragments but plainly signposts dependence on the Specified Amount and Coverage Option. Nothing ambiguous of substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.13, 2.14 and the two option paragraphs that follow. No conflict.
judgments.clause_name: 4.2 - Amount of Proceeds Payable at Death

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Option A is a "greater of" formula with two arithmetically specified limbs, including interest on premiums received since the prior Monthly Due Date. The mechanics are definite, though the corridor limb is intricate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 2.14, the risk-percentage table, and the following paragraph on riders and indebtedness. Its interaction with 5.9's reduction of the Specified Amount on withdrawal is expressly addressed there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Option B mirrors Option A with the account value added; the second limb contains only a typographical slip ("prior to our coinciding with"). No genuine second meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.14 and with 5.9's statement that under Option B the Specified Amount is unchanged but the death benefit falls with the account value. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Death benefits are "increased... by any premiums received after the date of death", which is an odd and arguably ambiguous direction given premiums are not owed after death. That phrase can be named as the problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.10(3) says any premium unpaid at death is deducted from the Proceeds, and 4.2 Option A already adds premiums received since the prior Monthly Due Date — the three treatments of post-death premium overlap awkwardly. That is a specific reconciliation point.
judgments.clause_name: 4.2 - Increases and decreases to death benefits

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurer may modify death benefits to comply with federal tax law, but the Owner "has the right to refuse any modification" — the consequence of refusal (loss of tax qualification, or no modification at all) is left unstated. That silence is a genuine construction gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.3 lets the insurer refuse or return excess premium to preserve qualification, so refusal of a benefit modification may frustrate that mechanism. The two tax-compliance tools are not squared with each other.
judgments.clause_name: 4.2 - Modification to comply with Federal tax laws

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest is at "an annual rate determined by us but never less than the rate required by the state in which the Insured resides" — the rate is unilaterally set subject only to a statutory floor, which is a definite if discretionary standard. "Until settlement" is also plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.2 and Section 10's interest floors; no other provision fixes interest on death proceeds. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula "A + B + C - D - E" is stated but the definitions of the letters are largely missing or scrambled, so the central account-value calculation cannot be performed from the text. That is a mechanical defect at the heart of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also mis-cites "Section 2" for the Monthly Insurance Charge (defined operatively in 5.3) and must be read with 5.6, 5.9 and 5.10, all of which depend on this value. The dependency chain makes the gap consequential.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The worked example is self-contradictory as printed: "the Policy Loan Interest Rate specified in Section 1 less two (2) percentage points (eg. 6% less 2 points equals 6%)". A parenthetical whose arithmetic does not work is a mechanical error that bears on the credited rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the guaranteed annual interest rate in Section 1 and with 9.3; if the loan rate less two points falls below the guaranteed floor, the two provisions pull apart. That is a specific, identifiable tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substance — a monthly deduction equal to the Cost of Insurance plus rider costs — is clear; the numbering and word order are garbled. Nothing ambiguous to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates 2.15 accurately and feeds 5.10's lapse test; the section is mislabelled "3.3" rather than 5.3, which is only a numbering slip. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is "A x (B - C)" but only A and B are defined in the surviving text, the trigger is stated as "any Premium Due Date" rather than the Monthly Due Date used everywhere else, and the guaranteed rates are said to be "per $1,050". Those are namable mechanical errors that change the calculation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Premium Due Date" is not a defined term in Section 2, which defines only "Monthly Due Date" (2.17), and 5.3 fixes the deduction to the Monthly Due Date. That mismatch is a specific internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The adjustment rule for special risk classes survives only as scattered words ("(a) For a flat... rating percentage; or (b) For a flat extra rating"), so neither adjustment can be applied. The provision is unreadable as an operative formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 identifies the risk class as "Standard", so the special-class adjustment may never bite here; nothing else in the policy contradicts it. No specific conflict.
judgments.clause_name: 5.4 - Adjustment of rates for special risk classes

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line pointer to Section 1 for rider charges, truncated but plain in intent. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.15 and 5.3, which include rider costs in the Monthly Insurance Charge, and with Section 1's Waiver of Deduction rider entry. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Cash Value is said to be "equal to:" but the equation joining A, B and C is missing, and item C (an interest differential over the preceding 12 months) is described without a sign or purpose. The reader cannot compute the value from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.7 and 5.9–5.10 all build on Cash Value, and Section 1's Percent of Surrender Fee schedule supplies B, so the gap propagates through the surrender and lapse machinery. That is a real coherence problem rather than a mere typo.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two-line subtraction, wholly definite. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.6, 5.7's use in 5.10 and 9.4. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The right to surrender at any time and the termination of all coverage are plain; the postponement sentence has lost its "six months" lead-in but the exception is intelligible. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with 3.4 (no reinstatement after surrender) and 4.1; the six-month postponement power sits against 4.1's flat promise to pay Surrender Value, but 4.1 is naturally read subject to this. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The maximum withdrawal sentence is broken ("at [least] $500 but no more than the Surrender Value less $25 and less the next Monthly Insurance Charges"), the Withdrawal Charge is "A + B + $25" with B undefined, and the recomputation of the first-year Surrender Fee "divided by the Percent of Surrender Fee" is arithmetically opaque. Multiple namable mechanical defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reduction of the Specified Amount under Option A must be squared with 6.2's minimum Specified Amount and with 4.2, and the withdrawal deduction feeds 5.1 and 5.10; those links are stated but strained. Moderate relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lapse trigger has lost words ("if the Surrender Value on a Monthly Due Date is not [sufficient to] pay the next Monthly Insurance Charges") and the 60-day Grace Period sentence is broken, so the precise condition and what must be paid to avoid lapse are open. "Payment of additional premium" without a stated amount is itself indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.4 states the lapse test differently (excess of Cash Value over total Policy Indebtedness insufficient for the next charges), and the final paragraph of 5.10 plus 3.2(2) create a two-year no-lapse override; harmonising the three requires work. This is the provision most likely to be litigated in a lapse dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As printed the notice must be mailed "at least 50 days before the end of the Grace Period" while the Grace Period itself is only 60 days, which would require notice within ten days of the missed date — a figure that is almost certainly a mis-scanned 30 and that changes the obligation. That is a namable mechanical error going to the notice duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 5.10's 60-day Grace Period and 7.4(10)'s special annual-report lapse notification, the timing of the insurer's warning duties does not line up cleanly. Notice adequacy is exactly where those provisions collide.
judgments.clause_name: 5.10(1) - Notice before end of Grace Period

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "If adequate premium is not paid by the end of the Grace Period, this Policy will terminate without value" is short and definite, though "adequate premium" takes its content from 5.10(1). The phrase "without value" is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 3.4, which permits reinstatement for five years using the values in effect at lapse, and against the two-year no-lapse paragraph — so "terminate without value" is not absolute. That is a specific reconciliation point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause deducts "any premium which remains unpaid on the date of death" from the Proceeds, but under a flexible-premium policy no premium is ever strictly "unpaid" — the amount owed is indeterminate on the face of the words. That is a namable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.2 conversely increases the death benefit by premiums received since the prior Monthly Due Date and after death, and 5.10(1) frames the shortfall as "the amount of premium that will be sufficient to continue the Policy"; the three treatments are not aligned. A court would have to harmonise them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The no-lapse test is garbled ("if the sum of the premiums paid to date, less any Partial Withdrawals, and less any Policy Indebtedness equals or exceeds one-twelfth of the Planned Periodic Premium on [an] annual basis multiplied by the number of months since the Policy Date"), and "the first 2 Policy years" against a monthly test leaves the cut-off arguable. The broken syntax affects the computation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides the lapse rule in the opening paragraph of 5.10 and overlaps but does not match 3.2(2)'s two-year premium test, which omits withdrawals and indebtedness. That mismatch between two tests of the same thing is a concrete incoherence.
judgments.clause_name: 5.10 - No lapse during first 2 Policy years

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional statutory-basis clause naming the 1958 CSO table and 4.5% reserve interest. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.6's floor of the minimum cash value required by the state of delivery. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain procedural right to request changes in writing. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2, 6.3 and 6.4's requirement of officer approval for changes outside the section. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in subordinating changes to the conditions that follow. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.12 and the increase/decrease paragraphs. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of four requirements, two of which turn on satisfaction "satisfactory to us" — a discretionary but conventional standard. The list is enumerated with no catch-all, so its scope is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.8's separate two-year contest period for increases and with 5.7 (Surrender Value). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence order is scrambled by OCR ("effective on the Monthly Due Date following our [approval]... shown on an addition to Section 1"), but the mechanism is recoverable. Little genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.7's definition of Effective Date pointing to 6.2 for Specified Amount changes. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite limit of one increase per 12 months, expressed permissively ("we may limit"). The permissive form is a small point but not an ambiguity of meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2(4)'s similar power over the number of additional premiums. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reverse-order application of decreases is definite, but the final sentence is cut off before stating the minimum amount that must remain in force. The truncation removes an operative limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1's Minimum Specified Amount and 5.9's parallel minimum supply the missing floor, so the instrument as a whole fills the gap. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only fragments survive: which option may be changed to which is lost, and the new Specified Amount is "the death benefit less the [Policy Account Value] as of the effective date of change" — as printed the direction of the change cannot be determined. That is a serious mechanical gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2.14 and 4.2, the arithmetic makes sense only for an A-to-B or B-to-A conversion in one direction, and 5.9 treats the two options quite differently on withdrawal. The provision does not clearly integrate with those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is definite: written request, officer signature for changes not provided for, endorsement required, no agent authority. Nothing ambiguous to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits comfortably with 7.1's entire-contract clause and 6.1. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "This Policy the application and any supplemental applications are the entire contract" is missing a comma but the enumeration is clear; consideration is stated as the application plus premium. Only a punctuation slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.4 (changes must be endorsed) and 7.1's second paragraph; also against Section 1's rider entries, which are part of the contract though not listed here. Mild integration question about riders and endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The representations-not-warranties rule and the requirement that any statement relied on be in a written application are standard and definite. "In the absence of fraud" is a recognised carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with 7.8's incontestability period and 7.6's suicide clause, both of which use the Issue Date; the interaction is conventional rather than contradictory. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision cites "Section 7.7. - Incontestability", but incontestability is Section 7.8 and 7.7 is Misstatement of Age and Sex; the Temporary Insurance Agreement limb is also broken mid-sentence. A wrong cross-reference plus a missing limb both bear on when coverage begins.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with 3.1's flat statement that there is no coverage until payment and with 2.7's definition of Effective Date, and the misdirected reference to 7.7/7.8 puts two different remedies in play. That is a concrete internal misalignment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-item enumerated list of report contents introduced by "at least the following information", so the list is a floor and its reach is not in doubt; item 10's lapse notification is expressed conditionally but intelligibly. Little namable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 10's projected-lapse notification overlaps with the pre-lapse notice duty in 5.10(1), and the two use different triggers and timing; in a lapse dispute the adequacy of notice would turn on reading them together. That is a specific pairing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated so that what will be sent and how often ("we will send you a [report] ... during the year") is missing, along with the charge standard "reasonable... as determined by us". The gap is in the object of the promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the function of 7.5 (illustrative report on request for a reasonable charge), which supplies the pattern. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as to trigger (written request), consideration (reasonable charge determined by us) and content (projected values). "Reasonable charge" is a familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.4's annual report and 5.2's rate-declaration power. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause runs "two years from the Issue Date" and limits liability to premium paid less indebtedness and withdrawals; "Issue Date" is not among the defined terms in Section 2, which defines Policy Date and Effective Date instead. That undefined date term is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.8 uses the same undefined "Issue Date" while 2.6, 2.7 and 7.2 build the policy's timeline on the Policy Date and Effective Date; the instrument therefore runs two date systems in parallel. That is a specific coherence point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The misstatement-of-age-and-sex adjustment survives only as disconnected phrases, so neither the trigger nor the adjustment formula can be read. As printed the provision cannot be applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2 cross-refers to "Section 7.7" as Incontestability, which is in fact this provision's number, compounding the confusion between the two remedies. Moderate relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The contest bar is qualified by "unless the Surrender Value is insufficient to cover the next Monthly Cost of Insurance", an unusual carve-out whose effect — reviving contestability on a lapse — is far from plain, and "Issue Date" is undefined. Both are namable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out interacts directly with 5.10's lapse mechanics and 3.4's reinstatement rights, and uses "Monthly Cost of Insurance" where 5.3 uses "Monthly Insurance Charge"; the provisions do not use a common vocabulary. That mismatch is specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite rule: increases become incontestable after two years in force during the Insured's lifetime. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2's increase machinery and with the first paragraph of 7.8. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line nonparticipation statement; definite. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cover page's "NONPARTICIPATING" designation and with 5.2's declared-rate mechanism. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is truncated ("you may exercise every [right] provided by your Policy if..."), and the two conditions make ownership rights contingent on there being no irrevocable beneficiary and no assignment — as printed all rights are lost if either exists, which is broader than intended. That over-breadth is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.3 says only that owner and revocable-beneficiary rights "are subject to any assignment", which is narrower than a total suspension of rights, and 8.4 addresses irrevocable beneficiaries similarly. The two are in mild tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Little more than the skeleton survives ("You may cha[nge]... will be effe[ctive]... payment made or other action taken by us"), so the notice and effectiveness rules cannot be read from the text. The gap is in the operative mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.3 and 8.4 supply the same pattern (effective when signed, no effect on prior action), so the instrument is internally consistent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: assignment permitted, not binding until written notice, insurer not responsible for validity, rights subordinated. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.1's condition that the Policy has not been assigned and with 8.4. No conflict beyond the mild point noted under 8.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain default rules: beneficiary as shown on the application, Owner if none named, proceeds paid to the beneficiary subject to the section. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.4's definition and 4.1's direction to pay Death Proceeds to the Beneficiary. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional survivorship cascade to the Owner and then to the Owner's executor or administrator. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.4's opening paragraph and 10.1's identification of the payee. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change is "effective upon the date your request was signed but will have no effect on any payment made or other action taken by us before we receive it" — a relation-back rule with a stated carve-out, which is definite though it can produce hard cases. Nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors 8.2's change-of-ownership rule and is consistent with 4.1. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated to "You may obtain a Policy [loan]... us is the only security needed", so the loan right and its conditions are not fully stated. The security sentence is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.2–9.4 supply the amount, interest and indebtedness rules; consistent with those. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The base amount available ("The amount [available is the ...] loan less:") is missing, so the maximum loan cannot be computed, and the two deductions appear with a stray line between them. A missing base figure is a material mechanical gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.7 (Surrender Value) and 5.2's loan-securing interest rate imply the intended base, and 9.4 governs the consequences; nothing contradicts the clause. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rate is "specified in Section [1]" with the reference lost, and the last sentence reads "the loan will be increased by the amount" without saying of what. Both are legible in intent but incomplete as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 does list a Policy Loan Interest Rate and 5.2 credits that rate less two points to the secured portion; the pieces fit. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of indebtedness and its deduction from proceeds are plain; the lapse sentence is expressed as "the excess of the Cash Value over the total Policy Indebtedness" being insufficient. Definite arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.10 states the same lapse test using "Surrender Value", which 5.7 defines as Cash Value less indebtedness — so the two agree in substance but a court would still be asked why two different formulations appear, and neither carries the two-year no-lapse carve-out. Modest relational tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is scrambled, splitting the payee definition from the election right, and the qualification "subject to Section 8" has uncertain reach over a payee who is a beneficiary. That cross-limitation is a namable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 governs beneficiary designation and change and 8.1 conditions owner rights; whether an irrevocable beneficiary can elect an option is not squarely answered. Moderate relational uncertainty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sum payment at claim settlement; definite despite the OCR break. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1 and 10.2. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence collapses two alternatives (payments for a specified period or of a specified amount) with a parenthetical about present value equalling the Proceeds, so the mechanism reads incoherently as printed. The 4% floor is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.2 says amounts will be determined using "our rates in effect at the time of settlement", which must be squared with this option's guaranteed 4% floor and the fixed-period table. That is a specific pairing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The illustrative figure "$6,384" is plainly a mis-set $6.38, a mechanical error in a rate quotation. The rest of the option is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The quoted guarantee of $6.77 per $1,000 for a male age 65 does not match the Payments for Life table, which shows 6.72 for age 65 with no certain period and 6.62 with five years certain. That is a concrete numerical inconsistency between text and table.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The joint-life option survives only in fragments, so the survivor payment level and the guarantee period are not stated. "Guaranteed rates will be furnished upon request" leaves the guarantee undocumented in the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Options 2, 3 and 5 all state minimum guarantees in the text or tables, so this option's deferral to rates "furnished upon request" is out of step with the rest of Section 10. Mild inconsistency of treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is broken ("unless the B[eneficiary] Designation limits withdrawals, any withdrawal must..."), leaving the withdrawal minimum unstated, though the 4% interest floor and the annual payment rule are clear. The missing withdrawal condition is a genuine gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.2's present-value rule and with 8.4's beneficiary designations, which are the source of any withdrawal restriction. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Our rates in effect at the time of settlement" is a definite standard, but paired with "the present value of the amounts to be paid will be equal to the Proceeds" the provision leaves unclear whether current or guaranteed rates control when they diverge. That is a namable tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Options 2, 3 and 5 each promise rates "never less than" a stated guarantee, and the two payment tables set floors; a flat rule that current rates govern would override those floors unless read subject to them. That is a specific conflict a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single informational sentence; nothing operative to construe. Definite.
